verses.note: Most Christian interpreters from the early church on have also read Jesus' use of the verse of his return in glory (Matthew 24:30; Revelation 1:7). The two readings are often combined: the enthronement Daniel describes is made visible to the world when Christ comes.
The cosmic signs prepare for the coming of the Son of Man in verse 26. Whether they describe the end of the world or the end of an age, they announce that God is acting decisively.

On the majority reading, the verse describes the visible, personal return of Christ in glory, the hope the Nicene Creed confesses when it says that Christ will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead.
The creeds confess that Christ will come again but set no date, following verse 32. The difficulty of verse 30 has pressed the church to read the chapter carefully rather than to speculate.
The return of Christ is certain in fact and uncertain in date. Every date-setter in the church's history has run against this verse.
The master will come, and his coming will be sudden. Readiness for Christ's return is expressed in wakefulness now.
